Project description
Third-cycle subject:  Engineering Mechanics
Within EU doctoral network F airCFD , this project will combine high-performance computing, experiments and artificial intelligence in non-Newtonian flows, with the aim of improving rheological characterisation and modelling. In particular, we will design a digital twin rheometer to reliably measure complex fluid parameters in time-varying and chaotic flows.
We will use modern AI techniques to exploit spatial patterns in the computational and experimental data and optimize parameter sensitivity. The researcher will join the dynamic Complex Fluids Research group , have access to the supercomputing facilities at KTH, the Swedish e-Science Research Centre ( SeRC ) and the excellent research environment FLOW .
Supervision: Outi Tammisola and Fredrik Lundell are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
Mobility rules  - Candidates must not have resided or conducted their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately preceding the recruitment date,
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge.

A suitable background for this position is a master's degree in engineering, mathematics or physics with a focus on fluid mechanics, computational or experimental methods, and/or applied mathematics.
In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach,
analyze and work with complex issues,
strong motivation for doctoral studies, ability to work independently, critical analysis as well as possessing good levels of cooperative and communicative skills.

After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.

Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed alongside humans to carry out complex coordinated tasks. In these settings, autonomous systems must handle strict spatial and temporal constraints while adapting in real time to supervisory commands, unexpected obstacles, and environmental disturbances. Project description
Third-cycle subject:  Computer Science
The PhD student will work within GEOMANIP, an ERC Starting Grant project that aims to revolutionize the robotic manipulation of deformable objects by uncovering and exploiting their fundamental geometric nature. GEOMANIP proposes a paradigm shift that integrates the differential geometric structure of deformable objects into novel continuum physics-inspired neural representations, serving as the bedrock of a physically-grounded manipulation pipeline encompassing perception, planning, and control. The PhD student will contribute to one or more of the following topics: theoretical foundations and geometric formalization, representation learning, robust perception and geometric state estimation,  robot policy learning and control.

253680.body:
BI Norwegian Business School’s Department of Law and Governance and Department of Communication and Culture invite applications for a four-year doctoral scholarship focusing on regulatory delearning and the governance of transformative technologies. The expected start date is 1 January 2027, or upon agreement.
Position details
Location: BI Norwegian Business School, Oslo, Norway
Position: One PhD candidate position, full time, fixed-term contract of 48 months
Doctoral programme: PhD specialisation in Communication at BI Norwegian Business School
Application deadline: 15 November 2026 at 23:59 CET
Expected start: 1 January 2027, or upon agreement
About REGULAIRE
The scholarship is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies), a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Coordinated by Professor Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich, with Professor Sebastian Schwemer as principal investigator at BI, the network brings together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities.
REGULAIRE studies how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators recognise emerging problems, test interventions, develop institutional capacities and share lessons across organisations and jurisdictions. You will join an international cohort with supervision across institutions, joint training and collaboration with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations.
The doctoral project
Regulation accumulates over time, but institutions’ capacity to revise or retire rules that no longer serve their purpose does not always keep pace. This doctoral project examines “regulatory delearning”: how institutions identify, revise or retire outdated obligations in response to technological change.
Focusing on the EU and EEA, you will investigate how different forms of regulation, from legislation to standards and soft law, influence delearning. You will examine the conditions and procedures for reviewing, amending and repealing rules, including review and sunset clauses, drawing on the EU’s Better Regulation framework and recent simplification initiatives. A central question is how institutions can adapt rules while preserving safeguards, accountability and legal certainty.
Possible approaches include legal analysis, comparative case studies, evidence from regulatory sandboxes and comparisons across technology sectors. The successful candidate will develop an independent PhD project within this theme and contribute to REGULAIRE’s research agenda. The project offers a focused route into law and regulation, governance research and the study of adaptive regulation.
Research environment and supervision
You will be affiliated with BI’s Department of Law and Governance and Department of Communication and Culture. Research in Law and Governance spans national and European regulation of markets and technology, digital and corporate governance, and the relationship between law, economics and public policy. Communication and Culture contributes expertise in communication technologies, online communities, digital transformation and the social legitimacy of technological change.
You will also join BI’s Nordic Centre for Internet and Society (NCIS), an interdisciplinary research centre studying how emerging internet technologies affect working life and society.
Your main supervisor will be Professor Sebastian Schwemer (BI), with Professor Christian Fieseler as co-supervisor at BI and Stefan Larsson at Lund University as the international academic co-supervisor. A sectoral mentor will support the secondment.
You will meet your main supervisor at least monthly and the full supervisory team at least four times a year. Your progress and training will be recorded in a personal Career Development Plan.
Training and secondment
Network training includes three residential summer schools, covering regulatory learning and foresight at TUM, methods and analytics at BI, and academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen. You will also take part in methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and annual network reviews. This training complements the coursework and other requirements of BI’s doctoral programme.
The project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment, providing opportunities to study how technology-governance bodies identify, update and retire outdated regulatory mandates. The host, timing and detailed arrangements will be confirmed with the supervisory team.
Your work
Refine the research questions and design with the supervisory team.
Collect, manage and analyse research material using methods appropriate to the project.
Complete a doctoral thesis and related research publications, and communicate findings to academic and practitioner audiences.
Participate in local and network training, cohort activities, reviews and practitioner engagement, including the summer schools and planned secondment.
Contribute to teaching or other career-promoting duties as part of the four-year appointment.

Your profile
Applicants must hold, or complete by the start date, a relevant two-year master’s degree or comparable qualification that meets BI’s PhD entry requirements . The qualifying degree must include thesis work, normally 15–30 ECTS, and applicants must have a grade point average of B or higher, equivalent to 4 on BI’s five-point scale. An MBA does not qualify for admission.
Relevant backgrounds include law, socio-legal studies, political science, public administration, science and technology studies, economics, or related social science and interdisciplinary fields.
Knowledge of technology regulation, EU or administrative law, or digital governance would be an advantage, as would an interest in regulatory reform and how institutions evaluate, revise and retire rules. Experience with legal analysis, case studies, interviews, or qualitative and quantitative analysis is welcome. You are not expected to have experience in all these areas.
We are looking for strong analytical and academic writing skills, the ability to work independently and systematically, and a willingness to collaborate across disciplines. Excellent written and spoken English and fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions below are required.
Employment and support
The appointment is a full-time, four-year position based in Oslo. The annual salary is currently NOK 623,200 gross and will be adjusted in accordance with applicable regulations. The position normally offers membership in BI’s collective pension scheme. Twenty-five per cent of working time is allocated to teaching or other career-promoting duties; 36 research months are funded through REGULAIRE.
MSCA funding also provides support for mobility and, where applicable, family allowances under the grant rules. BI will confirm the applicable arrangements as part of the employment terms. You will have access to the network’s research, training and networking activities.
MSCA eligibility
Applicants may be of any nationality. On the first day of MSCA employment, the selected candidate must meet the following conditions:
Not hold a doctoral degree. Applicants who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis are ineligible even if the degree has not yet been formally awarded.
Not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or study, in Norway for more than 12 months during the preceding 36 months. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent in a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are excluded.
Be enrolled in, or meet the conditions for timely enrolment in, BI’s doctoral programme.

Appointment is conditional on documentary verification of these conditions and fulfilment of BI’s admission requirements. See the official MSCA Doctoral Networks guidance for further information.
How to apply
Submit your application through the “Send application” button on this vacancy’s page in BI’s electronic recruitment system. Please consult BI’s PhD application guidance and upload the following:
A cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant qualifications, identifying REGULAIRE DC08.
A CV, including publications and other relevant research activities, where applicable.
An original five-page project proposal addressing this doctoral project, including the research topic, proposed methods, schedule and relevant literature. Any use of generative AI to produce text must be clearly stated and cited.
Bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and transcripts, with a Diploma Supplement or equivalent explanation of the study and grading system and eligibility for further study. Include other relevant certificates and transcripts.
At least two recommendation letters from relevant employers, professors or supervisors providing evidence of your research potential.
BI’s signed verification document .
Documentation of English proficiency, or an English test waiver application with supporting evidence, where required.
Certificates and the course approval form for previously completed doctoral courses, if you wish to request recognition of these courses.

Applicants still completing their master’s degree should upload their latest transcript and state their expected completion date. The qualifying degree must be completed before the appointment begins.
All application documents must be submitted through the electronic system, not by email. Documents received after the deadline will not be considered, except for the final master’s certificate where the degree is being completed shortly before the agreed start date. Applications cannot be revised after submission. Candidates may be asked for further information or invited to an interview.
English language requirements
BI normally accepts native English speakers, applicants with a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution, and applicants whose qualifying master’s degree was taught in English as meeting its English-language requirement. Other applicants must normally provide TOEFL or IELTS results, or apply for a waiver.
BI’s published minimum is IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 on the 0–120 scale, with results from the preceding two years. Consult BI’s PhD entry requirements for current score requirements, accepted documentation and reporting instructions. TOEFL results should be sent directly to BI using institution code 0529; IELTS copies are accepted when the TRF number is visible. GMAT or GRE may be requested in particular cases; BI will inform applicants if required.
Contact
For questions about REGULAIRE or this doctoral project, contact Professor Sebastian Schwemer at [email protected] .
For questions about the PhD specialisation in Communication, contact Associate Dean Professor Christian Fieseler at [email protected] .
For questions about admission requirements and the application process, contact BI’s PhD Administration at [email protected] . Further information about the network is available at REGULAIRE .
REGULAIRE is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, Grant Agreement No. 101312218.

Job description
Come join IMT Mines Alès, a prestigious “grande école” ranked among the top engineering schools both nationally and globally, located in Alès—a welcoming, livable city and the capital of the Cévennes region, where residents highly value the quality of life.
Founded in 1843, IMT Mines Alès currently has 1,400 students (including 250 international students) and 380 staff members. The school has three high-level scientific and technological research and teaching centers, working in the fields of materials and civil engineering (C2MA), the environment and risk management (CREER), and artificial intelligence and industrial and digital engineering (CERIS). It operates 12 technology platforms and has 1,600 partner companies. For more information: https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr
You will be affiliated with the Center for Research and Teaching in Environment and Risks (CREER) at IMT Mines Alès and the HSM research unit.
This work is part of the PREV’IA project, which focuses on understanding and forecasting water resources in the Pliocene-Quaternary aquifer of the Roussillon Plain and the Lez spring that supplies Montpellier with drinking water.
Your work will build upon an ongoing thesis within the UMR HSM (HYTAKE team), focusing on the sustainability of the karst water resource (Lez aquifer) supplying a Mediterranean metropolis (Montpellier) in the context of climate change.
Your mission:
Use emerging concepts in “Physics-Informed Machine Learning” (PIML) approaches to assess the potential benefits of synergy in hydrogeological modeling: (1) concept-based modeling on the one hand, and (2) neural networks informed by, or complemented with, physics on the other. The PIML (Physics Informed Machine Learning) approach is being developed along two lines: (i) Physics Informed Architecture (PIA): integration of physical knowledge into the model architecture (hidden layers); and (ii) Physics Informed Loss Function (PILF): combining physical modeling (differential equations) and black-box methods, merged into the cost function (regularization term). Both methods may be explored. The proposed models may be used to determine the evolution of certain hydrological variables in response to climate change.

You can find more information in the job description below:
https://partage.imt.fr/index.php/s/R3Dr7Cf2q8972tc

253737.body:
We are looking for a Doctoral student to become part of our team at the Division of Maritime Environmental Science at the Department of Environmental and Energy Sciences. Join us in a collaborative and dynamic environment and contribute to research on sustainable shipping and the marine environment.
About us
The Department of Environmental and Energy Sciences was established in 2026 and represents a clear and strategic consolidation of efforts in the environmental field, with links to both interdisciplinary research areas and collaboration with society, industry, and academia. Here, expertise and infrastructure are brought together to support new research initiatives, strengthen education, and develop competitive and sustainable solutions to some of the greatest environmental challenges of our time.
Your doctoral studies in Maritime Environmental Science will be carried out within a team with extensive experience in shipping and sustainable antifouling strategies, at an exciting time when new solutions are needed and regulations are rapidly evolving. We have strong collaboration with national and international research groups and established contacts with organizations and industrial partners.
About the research project
This doctoral student project on Sustainable Antifouling strategies will investigate ultrasound as a method to hinder marine organisms (biofouling) on ship hulls. The opportunities and challenges of ultrasound as antifouling method will be illustrated and evaluated from environmental and economical perspective. Ultrasound technology will be compared to existing and emerging antifouling alternatives. The project will perform studies of effects in marine ecosystems and result in recommendations on cost- and energy-efficient use of ultrasound as an antifouling measure without negatively impacting marine life.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Environmental engineering, Natural Sciences (ie Biology, Oceanography, Environmental- or Marine Sciences) or equivalent education in a related field
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Experience in practical and analytical work from lab or field.
Experience in collection of data, statistical analyses and presentation of results
You are a motivated and independent researcher with good analytical skills and has a strong commitment to scientific inquiry.
You are interested in finding solutions for challenges in connection to sustainability, marine environment and shipping and look forward to perform interdisciplinary research.
We also believe that you have a strong curiosity and a genuine wish to learn and develop your skills and knowledge further in the fields of research, research communication and project management.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience in experimental work and design, analytical work in lab and fieldwork in aquatic environment are considered meritorious
Experience in programming (e.g., R, Matlab or Python) and demonstrated proficiency in the use of statistical tools are considered meritorious

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Maritime Environmental Science  (länk till specifik graduate school  Graduate schools | Chalmers  )
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing
The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours
Project specific tasks for the position include experimental and analytical work, field measurements, data processing, presentation of results to a diverse audience including environmental agencies, industry and academia and publication writing

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  October 31st, 2026
For questions, please contact:
Lena Grenhag, associate professor
[email protected]
We look forward to your application!

Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. 253741.body:
Ämnesområde
Miljökonsekvensanalys
Ämnesbeskrivning
Ämnet miljökonsekvensanalys omfattar teoretisk, metodologisk och tillämpad forskning om miljöbedömning av projekt, planer och program. Kärnan är att utveckla och kritiskt granska hur miljöaspekter integreras i planerings- och beslutsprocesser för att främja hållbar utveckling, med fokus på såväl innehåll som praktisk tillämpning. Detta innefattar analys av hur kunskap, metoder och verktyg används i olika skeden av processen, samt hur dessa påverkar beslutsfattande, genomförande och uppföljning. Genom användning av olika kvalitativa och kvantitativa miljösystemanalytiska och beslutsstödjande verktyg, tillgängliggörs ekologisk, klimatrelaterad och annan hållbarhetskritisk kunskap för planeringen.
Forskningen bedrivs i en kontext där såväl svenska som internationella perspektiv är centrala. Samverkan med offentlig sektor och näringsliv är avgörande för forskningens relevans och genomförande. Med ökande fokus på nya hållbarhetsutmaningar, exempelvis med koppling till klimatanpassning, digitalisering, cirkulära lösningar och rättvisa, bidrar ämnet till att utveckla framtida arbetssätt, integrerade planeringsprocesser och kunskap för hållbar samhällsbyggnad.
Arbetsuppgifter
I arbetsuppgifterna ingår att bedriva undervisning, kursutveckling och examination på grundläggande och avancerad nivå inom ämnesområdet samt närliggande ämnen. Lektorn förväntas aktivt bidra till utvecklingen av kurser och utbildningsprogram vid institutionen, samt bidra med relevant samhällsanknytning för studentgrupperna inom dessa. Det är även av stor vikt att undervisningen bedrivs i nära koppling till aktuell forskning för att bidra till en forskningsanknuten utbildningsmiljö. Undervisningen, inklusive handledning av examensarbeten, bedrivs på både svenska och engelska och omfattar initialt cirka 50 % av anställningen, men anpassas efter institutionens behov. Även arbetsledning och administration inom undervisning kan ingå.
Inom forskning ingår att bedriva egen forskning inom ämnesområdet samt att aktivt söka och erhålla externa forskningsmedel. Lektorn förväntas bidra till institutionens utveckling och den akademiska miljön genom att initiera och delta i forskningssamarbeten i nära samverkan med andra forskargrupper inom institutionen och med andra delar av KTH. Samverkan med externa aktörer, nationellt och internationellt, samt från näringsliv och offentlig sektor är en viktig del i forskningens förankring, utveckling och nyttiggörande. Lektorn förväntas bygga upp och långsiktigt utveckla en självständig, internationellt erkänd forskningsverksamhet. I arbetsuppgifterna ingår även söka extern finansiering för samt att handleda doktorander och postdoktorer.
I anställningen ingår även att aktivt delta i det akademiska arbetet vid institutionen, skolan och KTH, inklusive att åta sig förtroendeuppdrag samt ansvars- och ledningsuppdrag inom institutionen. Lektorn förväntas även bidra till institutionens vision att ha en ledande roll i uppfyllandet av KTH:s mål inom hållbar utveckling och klimat.
Behörighet
Behörig att anställas som lektor är den som har:
avlagt doktorsexamen eller har motsvarande vetenskaplig kompetens eller någon annan yrkesskicklighet som är av betydelse med hänsyn till anställningens ämnesinnehåll och de arbetsuppgifter som ska ingå i anställningen, och
visat pedagogisk skicklighet.

Bedömningsgrunder
Som bedömningsgrunder vid anställning som lektor vid KTH ska graden av sådan skicklighet som är ett krav för behörighet för anställning gälla. Därutöver gäller de bedömningsgrunder som anges i avsnitt 1.2. i KTH:s anställningsordning i förhållande till fastställd anställningsprofil.
Det är av högsta betydelse att den sökande har visat
vetenskaplig skicklighet inom miljökonsekvensanalys.
pedagogisk skicklighet inom miljökonsekvensanalys, visat bland annat genom erfarenhet av individuell handledning på grundläggande nivå och forskarnivå.
förmåga att verka inom ämnet i både en svensk och internationell kontext.
förmåga att undervisa på svenska.

Det är av näst högsta betydelse att den sökande har visat
samarbetsförmåga.
förmågan att samverka med det omgivande samhället för ömsesidigt utbyte och ha verkat för att den kunskap och kompetens som finns vid universitetet kommer samhället till nytta.

Det är även av betydelse att den sökande har visat
skicklighet att utveckla och leda verksamhet och personal. Däri ingår att ha kunskap om mångfalds- och likabehandlingsfrågor med särskilt fokus på jämställdhet.
administrativ skicklighet.

Fackliga representanter
Du hittar kontaktuppgifter på KTH:s webbsida.
Ansökan
Utforma din ansökan enligt KTH:s cv-mall . Du som sökande har ansvaret för att ansökan är komplett utifrån annonsen och cv-mallen. Komplett ansökan ska vara KTH tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdagen vid midnatt, CET/CEST.
Du ansöker online via KTH:s rekryteringssystem.
För mer information om bedömning, se Anställningsordning vid KTH.
Övrigt
För information om behandling av personuppgifter i samband med rekrytering läs mer här.
Det kan förekomma att en anställning hos KTH är placerad i säkerhetsklass. Om så är fallet för just denna anställning görs en säkerhetsprövning av sökande i enlighet med säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) efter samtycke. I dessa fall är en förutsättning för anställning att sökande blir godkänd efter säkerhetsprövning.
Vi undanber oss kontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av jobbannonser.

Bli en del av KTH

KTH formar framtiden genom utbildning, forskning och innovation. Som ett ledande internationellt tekniskt universitet spelar vi en aktiv roll i att driva och medverka i omställningen till ett hållbart samhälle. Här erbjuds du möjligheten att växa och utvecklas på en kreativ och dynamisk arbetsplats med goda arbetsvillkor och förmåner. Jämställdhet, mångfald och lika villkor är en kvalitetsfråga och en självklar del av KTH:s värdegrund som universitet och statlig myndighet.

253810.body:
RobotX PhD Fellowship 2027
RobotX, the Center for Robotics at ETH Zurich, is looking for outstanding doctoral students who want to build robots that work in the real world. With the RobotX PhD Fellowship 2027, you apply once and are considered by several RobotX research groups across ETH Zurich. You choose up to three professors you would like to work with, and they review your application.

Application deadline: 27 November 2026.

Job description
The research groups of RobotX cover a broad spectrum of robotics, including but not limited to:

Soft and Musculoskeletal Robotics: bioinspired robots built from compliant materials, artificial muscles, and tendons, for safe and adaptive interaction with an unstructured world.

Robotic Locomotion and Manipulation: legged robots, robot arms, and hands that move and act reliably in complex terrain and contact-rich tasks.

Biohybrid Robots: robots built from living cells, engineered tissue, and synthetic materials, actuated by muscle and powered by chemical energy.

Perception and Computer Vision: 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and scene understanding that give robots reliable perception of their surroundings.

Human-Robot Interaction: sensory-motor interaction between humans and machines for assistive, rehabilitative, and cooperative tasks.

Computational Design and Fabrication: simulation, optimization, and learned surrogate models to design and fabricate efficient, bioinspired robots.

Reinforcement Learning and Machine Learning: data-driven methods that let robots learn new skills and adapt to new tasks and environments.

Humanoid Robotics and Tactile Sensing for Manipulation: humanoid loco-manipulation, whole-body control, and tactile sensing that let robots reason across touch and vision to handle objects dexterously.

Motion Planning and Control: algorithms for navigation, control, and decision-making in dynamic environments.

Safety-Critical Robotic Systems: robots that perform reliably under uncertainty, in particular when they work alongside humans.

You define your doctoral project together with your supervisor during your first months.

Profile

A Master's degree in mechanical or electrical engineering, computer science, robotics, bioengineering, materials science, or a closely related field, completed by August 2027

An excellent academic record in both your Bachelor's and Master's studies

Demonstrated experience in one or more of the research areas above, ideally a project you carried from idea to a working result on real hardware

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the drive to do independent research

Strong programming skills; experience with robotics software frameworks is a plus

Excellent written and spoken English

We offer

A fully funded doctoral position at ETH Zurich, employed at the ETH doctoral salary rate with full social benefits

Supervision by a RobotX professor and access to the RobotX network of robotics groups across ETH Zurich

Start date by agreement in 2027

Your career with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society.

We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university .

You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ, childcare and attractive pension benefits.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application as one merged PDF file, ideally under 10 MB, with the documents in this order:

Cover letter: your research motivation, what you have built so far, and which RobotX research groups you want to work with and why

CV, including any publications or preprints

Transcripts of your Bachelor's and Master's degrees in English, with the local grading scale

Names and contact details of three references, each with an email address and a direct phone number

One publication, thesis, or project report that shows your research and writing

Name the PDF with the application date (YYMMDD) and your last and first name. For example, Jane Miller applying on 1 December 2026 names her file 261201_MillerJane_application.pdf .

Further information about RobotX can be found on our website . Questions regarding the fellowship should be directed to Ms. Isabella De Nitti, [email protected] (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

253834.body:
Reference number ORU 2.1.1-05769/2026
Örebro University and the School of Science and Technology are looking for a doctoral student (PhD student) for the doctoral programme in Computer Science, concluding with a doctoral degree.
Start date: 1st of December 2026
Project description
The multi-disciplinary center for cyber resilient AI, RESIST, is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI and cybersecurity to develop novel solutions to cyber resilient AI for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a role model in secure trustworthy AI by pioneering cyber resilience across the AI lifecycle. The research program focuses on four key themes: Trustworthy and Verifiable AI, Runtime Security Assurance, Robust and Secure AI-Supported Development, and Resilient Distributed and Agentic AI. RESIST will drive world-class research in the intersection between AI and cybersecurity through a strong, stimulating and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. RESIST will also serve as a national hub for cyber resilient AI, promoting education, knowledge sharing, and policy development.
This PhD position is associated with the research theme Resilient Distributed and Agentic AI. For systems with multiple agents – robots, AI agents or humans, we will look at their interactions and analyze whether we can use explicit interaction protocols as a basis to secure interaction on a higher level than communication frameworks. Such high-level negotiation protocols can be pre-defined or learnt, yet they also need to capture flexibility in exchanging information or giving instructions for modelling modern multi-agent workflows. Research will concern the generation of explicit interaction protocols adapted to the agents involved, as well as the generation of execution guards from those learnt protocols. The overall goal is to make interaction robust, safe, and secure. Also, testing and evaluation in realistic, sandboxed environments as well as in real operational contexts is part of the project. Research is tightly integrated with other research themes within the center.
Supervision: The doctoral student will be supervised by Prof. Amy Loutfi (primary), Prof. Franziska Klügl (secondary) and Dr. Alberto Giaretta (secondary).
The programme and the doctoral studentship
The doctoral programme consists of courses and an independent research project that you will present in a doctoral thesis. The programme concludes with a doctoral degree and comprises 240 credits, which corresponds to four years of full-time study.
Our ambition is for your doctoral studies to be stimulating and purposeful throughout the programme until you have obtained your doctoral degree. A thorough introduction will therefore get you off to a good start and provide a solid foundation on which you can build your studies. As a doctoral student at Örebro University, you will be offered a specially tailored seminar series, covering matters ranging from doctoral programme rules and careers to support during the study period and networking.
The place on the programme is linked to a full-time doctoral studentship for the duration of the study programme, which corresponds to four years of full-time study. More information on doctoral studentships, part-time studies and part-time doctoral studentships can be found in the  Regulations Handbook . The initial salary for a doctoral studentship is SEK 32,300 a month (salary period 2025/2026).
Entry requirements and selection
For admission to doctoral studies, applicants are required to meet both  general entry requirements  and specific entry requirements. In addition, applicants must be considered in other respects to have the ability required to benefit from the programme. For a full account of the entry requirements, refer to the  admissions regulations  as well as to annex 2 to the general syllabus for Computer Science.
Applicants meet the general entry requirements if they
have been awarded a second-cycle qualification,
have satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or
have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Applicants meet the specific entry requirements for doctoral studies in Computer Science if they have been awarded a Degree of Master of Science in Engineering or a one-year Master’s degree from a programme within the subject field or related subjects, or if he or she has received a passing grade of at least 120 credits, including an independent project of at least 15 credits, in a main field of study of relevance to the computer science field. At least 30 credits of the 120 credits must have been awarded in the second cycle. A person who has acquired substantially corresponding knowledge, in Sweden or abroad, also meets the specific entry requirements.
Information
For more information about the programme and the doctoral studentship, please contact Prof. Amy Loutfi, email:  [email protected] , and/or Prof. Franziska Klügl, email: [email protected] or Dr. Alberto Giaretta, email: [email protected] . For administration issues, contact Head of Unit Martin Magnusson, email: [email protected] .
At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.
Örebro University actively pursues equal opportunities and gender equality as well as a work environment characterized by openness, trust and respect. We value the qualities that diversity adds to our operations.
Application to the programme and for the doctoral studentship
The application is made online. Click the button “Apply” to begin the application procedure.
For the application to be complete, the following electronic documents must be included:
CV
Proof that you meet the general and specific entry requirements (copies of the original certificate and official transcript for bachelor's and master's degrees)
Independent project (degree project)
Other relevant documents, course and degree certificates verifying eligibility
Description of research interests - explaining why you are interested in this project and why you would be a good candidate for the role (1 page)

As a main rule, application documents and attachments are to be written in Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, or English. Certificates and documents in other languages verifying your qualifications and experience must be translated by an authorised translator to Swedish or English. A list of authorised translators can be obtained from  Kammarkollegiet  (the Legal, Financial and Administrative Services Agency),  www.kammarkollegiet.se/engelska/start .
When you apply for admission, you automatically also apply for a doctoral studentship.
More information for applicants will be found on our career site:  https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/
The application deadline is 2 November 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!
As we have already made our choices in terms of external collaboration partners and marketing efforts for this recruitment process, we decline any contact with recruitment agencies and advertisers.
As directed by the National Archives of Sweden ( Riksarkivet ), we are required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

253913.body:
How do advanced composite materials perform after millions of load cycles in the demanding environment of an aeroengine? As a doctoral student in this international research collaboration, you will help answer that question through a combination of experimental testing, advanced simulations, and close interaction with leading researchers and industry experts. Your work will contribute to the development of future aerospace structures that are lighter, more efficient, and more reliable.
About us
The PhD position is placed at the Division of Computational Mechanics and Materials Engineering . We foster an inclusive, friendly, and helpful work environment to which we welcome you to contribute. Our activities integrate computational mechanics and advanced materials technology, combining multidisciplinary expertise to predict, understand, and elevate the performance of engineering materials and structures.
Within the project, you will be supported by an international team of experts in the area of mechanics of composites, combining academic excellence with industrial expertise and experience.
About the research project
The project aims to enable the deployment of advanced composite structures in aeroengines by developing reliable methods for predicting fatigue life of textile carbon fibre composites under thermomechanical tension-tension loading. Through combined experimental characterisation and development of an industrially applicable simulation framework, the project will support safe and efficient design of complex aerospace components.
More specifically, the project goals are to:
Characterise the fatigue properties and stiffness degradation of a relevant prototype textile reinforced composite material system under pure cyclic tension-tension loading.
Develop an industrially applicable and computationally efficient ply-level macroscale fatigue model that describes how damage evolves under varying load amplitudes and thermal conditions.
Combine the novel ply-level fatigue model with an existing state-of-the-art inter-laminar fatigue damage model into a complete fatigue life assessment framework.
Accelerate the computational efficiency of the framework by utilising novel cycle extrapolation techniques to represent the effect of fatigue loading over many cycles at a time.
Evaluate realistic but critical thermomechanical fatigue cycles through a combined experimental-simulation approach.
Enable industrial adoption of the proposed fatigue assessment framework into future design procedures at GKN Aerospace.

Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in  Applied Mechanics, Structural Engineering, Computational Engineering, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics or similar.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Documented experience (education/courses or thesis project with high grades) in continuum mechanics, advanced finite element method and the mechanics of fibre-reinforced polymers
Interest and high skills in programming and numerical methods

*for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
We also expect that you are analytical, ambitious, independent, and a strong team player that thrives through collaboration.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Documented knowledge in experimental testing.
Documented knowledge in aerospace applications and/or aeroengines.
Documented knowledge and experience in ANSYS or LS Dyna, including implementation of user subroutines (such as user materials or user elements)

What you will do
Characterise the thermoemechanical tension-tension fatigue behaviour of a prototype composite materials sytem with textile reinforcements.
Develop and implement a complete numerical framework to assess the tension-tension fatigue life of aeroengine components.
Develop your scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research through written scientific publications and oral presentations at international conferences.
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Solid and Structural Mechanics .
Teach on Chalmers' undergraduate level corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Project

The proposed PhD project "Optimizing Digital Uptake: An Interdisciplinary Evaluation of Blended Micro-Certifications for Frontline Extension in Ethiopia" forms part of the VLIRUOS TEAM project EQUIP, in which Arba Minch University (AMU), KU Leuven and Arba Minch College of Teacher Education (AMCTE) collaborate to strengthen the professional practice of Health Extension Workers (HEWs) and Development Agents (DAs) in Southern Ethiopia through inclusive, low-bandwidth digital and blended learning. EQUIP will establish a Digital Learning Hub at Arba Minch University, co-create health and agriculture micro-certifications with the Gamo Zone bureau, and test offline-first learning approaches designed for remote and low-connectivity settings. Gender, location and other barriers to participation will be addressed through the PROGRESS-Plus equity framework and iterative design-based research.

The PhD candidate will lead an equity-adaptive design-based research program examining which combinations of instructional design, motivational design, low-bandwidth technology and field coaching produce meaningful learning and sustained changes in frontline practice. The PhD candidate will work across the health–agriculture–education nexus and will help translate evidence into institutional standards, micro-certification design, Continuing Professional Development (CPD) recognition and implementation guidance.

The final research questions and methods will be refined with the selected PhD candidate and supervisors, reviewed by the Scientific Quality Cell, and submitted for the required scientific, ethics and data-protection approvals. The approved project anticipates iterative prototyping, mixed-method evaluation, disaggregated learning analytics and field-based competency assessment across selected Gamo Zone woredas.

The main responsibilities of the candidate will be to

develop a rigorous doctoral proposal and equity-adaptive design-based research protocol

conduct literature review, stakeholder/needs assessment and baseline research

obtain and comply with ethics, informed-consent and data-protection approvals

coordinate iterative design, pilot, evaluation and redesign cycles for the health and agriculture micro-certification tracks

evaluate access, usability, learning, competency gain and application in frontline practice, with attention to gender and remote locations

work with HEWs, DAs, zonal supervisors/Field Coaches, AMU/AMCTE staff, technical teams and policy partners

integrate quantitative, qualitative and learning-analytics evidence

contribute scientifically to the project’s behavioral-change, credential-value, cost and sustainability questions

coordinate research linkages with four MSc projects and support MSc researchers (without replacing their supervisors)

produce timely progress reports, peer-reviewed manuscripts, conference contributions, policy/practice briefs, open research outputs where appropriate, and a doctoral thesis

contribute to the Digital Learning Hub, E-learning Champion training and project learning events

comply with AMU, KU Leuven and VLIRUOS research-integrity, safeguarding, financial, visibility and scholarship requirements

Profile

The applicant must

preferably be a permanent AMU academic staff member, appointment and continued institutional affiliation must be verifiable

hold a relevant master’s degree in Computer Science or related fields

meet the applicable academic admission requirements of AMU including NGAT and the agreed KU Leuven doctoral/visiting doctoral route

demonstrate research readiness through a strong master’s record, thesis/research experience and a feasible concept note

demonstrate aptitude and genuine interest in digital pedagogy, adult learning and inclusive low-bandwidth design

be able to conduct interdisciplinary mixed-method research and work respectfully with non-academic stakeholders and rural frontline workers

have a sufficient command of English for doctoral research and international collaboration, and be willing to provide any formal evidence or training required by the doctoral authorities

be available for the full doctoral trajectory and for the approved research stays in Belgium (6 months in Activity Year 1, 12 months in Activity Year 3 and 6 months in Activity Year 5, subject to admission, visa and mobility administration)

obtain a signed AMU/department commitment for meaningful study leave from normal academic/administrative duties, continued employment/salary and reintegration/retention during and after the doctorate

pass the eligibility (CGPA, Publication, interview and/or written) exam to be administered by the project as per the Grant and Collaborative Projects guidelines of AMU

be eligible for a VLIRUOS project scholarship, including the applicable institutional-affiliation and nationality requirements

Desirable Experience :

Design-based research, implementation research or program evaluation

Mixed-method study design, statistics and qualitative analysis

Adult learning, instructional design, e-learning, HCI/UX or educational technology

Working with health or agriculture extension systems and public-sector stakeholders

Affinity with gender, inclusion, PROGRESS-Plus or other equity analysis

Mobile/offline digital tools, LMS data or learning analytics

Research ethics, secure data management and reproducible research

Peer-reviewed publication, policy communication or supervision/mentoring

Project coordination and ability to deliver across disciplines and institutions

Note: No single applicant is expected to be an expert in every desirable area. The committee will assess research potential, thematic fit, learning ability and the strength of the complete profile.

Offer

Scholarship and Institutional Support

The selected scholar will remain an AMU staff member. AMU’s agreed employment, salary and study leave arrangements will apply while the scholar conducts research in Ethiopia.

During approved research stays in Belgium, the current budget provides a research scholarship allowance of EUR 1,900 per month, subject to the applicable VLIRUOS framework and final scholarship administration.

The approved project budget provides financing for a research stay of 24 months in Belgium spread across three mobilities and includes budgeted international travel. Scholarship and travel payments remain subject to admission, registration, visa, mobility and financial procedures.

Approved project research and fieldwork costs in Ethiopia will be covered according to the project work plan and financial rules. There is no separate local PhD stipend in the approved budget.

The scholarship allowance is a compensation for living costs during the approved stays in Belgium.

The researcher will receive joint scientific supervision from AMU and KU Leuven, access to the EQUIP research network and appropriate project facilities.

The application should include the following documents in order :
1. Cover page with name, AMU Faculty/department, Staff ID, contact details, and document checklist
2. Motivation letter, maximum two pages
3. Curriculum vitae, including education, employment, research, publications/outputs, methods/software, teaching, service, languages, and two referees
4. Concept note of 1,500-2,000 words excluding references and containing the
* Problem statement and relevance to EQUIP
* Proposed research questions
* Conceptual/design-based research approach
* Proposed quantitative and qualitative methods
* Gender, location, and inclusion considerations
* Ethics and data-protection considerations
* Expected scientific and practical outputs
* High-level four-to-five-year work plan aligned with the three stays in Belgium
5. Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates and complete transcripts
6. Master’s thesis abstracts plus one sample publication
7. Evidence of current permanent AMU employment
8. Signed faculty/department/unit head letter confirming in-principle study leave, continued employment/salary, and reintegration
9. Available evidence of English proficiency
10. Signed declaration of accuracy, availability, conflicts of interest, and consent to process application data

The following selection procedure will be applicable :

Administrative eligibility screening against the mandatory criteria

Independent scoring of eligible written applications by the joint selection panel using the published criteria and as per AMU grant and collaborative projects guidelines

Shortlisted candidates complete a short research/methods exercise and give a structured presentation/interview online or at AMU

References, credentials, employment status and institutional-study leave feasibility are verified

The joint committee records a ranked recommendation. The Project Steering Committee endorses the final selection as required by the approved proposal; university admission remains with the competent academic authorities

Selection remains conditional on AMU and KU Leuven academic admission, the applicable scholarship/visa route and final institutional approvals

Disclaimer
AMU and KU Leuven are committed to a fair, transparent and inclusive call process. Female applicants and qualified staff from groups or locations under-represented in research leadership are strongly encouraged to apply. The same merit criteria will be applied to all candidates; where candidates are substantially equal, the project’s approved gender and inclusion commitments may be used as a documented tie-break in accordance with applicable policy.

Interested?

For more information please contact Dr. Mohammed Abebe, mail: [email protected] , Prof. dr. Wim Van Petegem, mail: [email protected] or Prof. dr. ir. Koen Eneman, mail: [email protected] .

Doctoral Position in Risk-Based Inspection and Maintenance Planning of Tunnels
The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a doctoral student. This position focuses risk-based inspection and maintenance planning for tunnels, including probabilistic risk updating, Value of Information analysis, and intervention program optimisation. This position is part of an interdisciplinary SNSF project in collaboration with the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, the Hagerbach Test Gallery, and the EuroTube Foundation.

The preferred starting date is 1 February 2027, although other dates are negotiable.

Project background
Tunnels are critical links in transport networks, and many Swiss road and rail tunnels are ageing while being subject to increasing traffic loads, climate-related stressors, and evolving safety requirements. Their maintenance involves two interdependent asset domains, namely structural elements, such as lining, portals, and drainage, and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, such as ventilation, lighting, and fire detection. In current practice, these domains are managed largely in isolation, inspections remain heavily manual, and evidence from different campaigns, sensors, and specialists is fragmented across separate reports and databases. Interventions are therefore often planned using disjointed evidence and conservative heuristics, even where substantial data exist.

The project Predictive, Resilient, Integrated Systems for Management of Tunnel (PRISM-T), funded by the SNSF, addresses this challenge through an integrated digital twin workflow for tunnel maintenance decision support. Heterogeneous inspection and monitoring evidence is transformed into uncertainty-aware condition indicators, which are used to update risk, to assess whether additional information is worth collecting, and to derive executable intervention programs. Extended reality (XR) is used to validate decisions and to guide inspection and maintenance work on site.

The workflow is developed and validated in the Tunnel Digitalisation Centre of the Hagerbach Test Gallery in Flums, and its transferability is tested at the DemoTube facility of the EuroTube Foundation in Dübendorf. Regular field work at both sites and close collaboration with the partner team in Bolzano form an integral part of the doctoral research.

Within this project, the doctoral position addresses the decision layer of the workflow, in which maintenance decision processes are formalised and uncertainty-aware condition indicators, developed in a companion doctoral position, are used to update risk and to optimise intervention programs under realistic tunnel constraints.

Job description
The successful candidate will map and formalise current tunnel maintenance decision processes for the structural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing domains through workshops and interviews with practitioners. On this basis, risk and consequence models based on Bayesian networks will be formulated, and incremental risk updating methods will be developed. A computationally tractable Value of Information analysis will be developed using approximation strategies, such as surrogate models and scenario reduction. Intervention program optimisation models accounting for sequencing, bundling, access windows, and resource constraints will be formulated and solved, with outputs traceable to the underlying evidence. The candidate will contribute to validation campaigns at the Hagerbach Test Gallery and the EuroTube Foundation.

Profile

A Master’s degree in civil engineering, operations research, industrial engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field

A strong background in probabilistic modelling, reliability and risk analysis, and mathematical optimisation

Very good programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with optimisation solvers

Familiarity with infrastructure asset management, Bayesian networks, decision analysis, Value of Information analysis, or business process modelling would be considered an advantage

Willingness to carry out field work in underground environments and to collaborate within an interdisciplinary and international team

Proficiency in written and spoken English is required, and knowledge of German is regarded as an asset

We invite applications for two Doctoral positions in experimental quantum computing with superconducting circuits. You will work in the stimulating research environment of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology ( WACQT ), a 12-year initiative started in 2018 with the purpose of advancing Swedish academia and industry to the forefront of quantum technology. The core project of the centre is to build a quantum computer based on superconducting circuits. You will be part of the Quantum Computing group  in the Quantum Technology Laboratory (QTL) division of the Microtechnology and Nanoscience (MC2) department, working in a large team of PhDs, postdocs and researchers.
About us
The Department of Microtechnology and Nanoscience advances the frontiers in quantum technology, nanoscience, photonics and future electronic systems - for technical and societal development. Our cross-disciplinary approach gives interesting collaborations in academy, industry and society, and is a driving force for innovations, results and breakthroughs. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.
At the Quantum Technology Laboratory , we explore how quantum physics can unlock radically new ways of processing information - far beyond the limits of classical systems. Our research spans quantum computing, sensing, transduction, thermodynamics, and foundations, all aimed at harnessing the powerful behavior of light and matter at the quantum level. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.

253989.body:
A full-time PhD position is available for an enthusiastic and highly motivated researcher to develop artificial intelligence methods for the multimodal analysis of chronic liver disease and liver cancer. The position is based in the Govaere Research Group at the Department of Imaging & Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, KU Leuven, and is embedded in a close collaboration with Prof. Jeroen Dekervel, with co-supervision by Prof. Asier Antoranz.

The Govaere Research Group is part of the Laboratory of Translational Cell and Tissue Research and is fully embedded in the pathology department at KU Leuven and University Hospitals Leuven. We study chronic liver disease using patient-derived tissue, digital pathology and molecular profiling, with strong links to hepatology, oncology, pathology, radiology and computational biology. The group is also connected to the KU Leuven Institute for Single Cell Omics (LISCO).

https://govaerelab.com/

Website unit

Project

The project aims to develop and validate AI models that combine information from digitised histopathology slides with molecular datasets to predict biologically and clinically relevant features of liver disease. Where suitable datasets are available, MRI-derived information may also be incorporated to extend the approach towards multimodal prediction.

The research will span the inflammation-to-cancer continuum, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), alcohol-associated steatohepatitis (ASH) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Rather than focusing on a single cell type or disease stage, the project will investigate how tissue morphology, molecular programmes and imaging phenotypes jointly capture disease mechanisms, progression and heterogeneity (reference Boesch M et al Nature Genetics 2026).

Research will include:

Curation, quality control and harmonisation of whole-slide images and linked clinical and molecular datasets.

Development of computational pathology workflows using deep learning, self-supervised learning, foundation models and/or multiple-instance learning.

Integration of image-derived features with transcriptomic, spatial-omics, genomic, proteomic or other molecular profiles.

Exploration of multimodal models incorporating radiological data, particularly MRI, where appropriate.

Biological interpretation and visualisation of model predictions in close interaction with pathologists, clinicians and molecular researchers.

Robust evaluation of model performance, generalisability and interpretability using reproducible and well-documented computational workflows.

Key tasks

Complete a doctoral training programme and conduct original research leading to a PhD in AI and digital pathology for chronic liver disease and HCC.

Develop, train and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning models for whole-slide pathology and multimodal biomedical data.

Work with large, heterogeneous datasets and contribute to data preprocessing, quality control, annotation and documentation.

Collaborate closely with researchers and specialists in pathology, hepatology, oncology, radiology, molecular biology and biomedical AI.

Communicate progress and results to the supervisory team and present findings at national and international scientific meetings.

Prepare scientific manuscripts and contribute to collaborative research outputs and funding applications where appropriate.

Contribute to the wider academic environment, for example by supporting master’s students or educational activities.

Profile

Essential:

You hold a master's degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics or a closely related field.

You have strong programming skills, preferably in Python;  proficiency in R is an additional asset.

A solid foundation in machine learning, deep learning, statistics or data science.

Motivation to work at the interface of AI, pathology and translational liver research, and commitment to completing a doctorate within four years.

Excellent spoken and written English.

Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary team.

Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills.

Desirable:

Experience in computer vision, digital pathology or whole-slide image analysis.

Experience with self-supervised learning, vision or multimodal foundation models, multiple-instance learning, image-omics integration or explainable AI.

Familiarity with molecular or spatial-omics analysis, multimodal data integration, radiomics or MRI analysis.

Prior knowledge of pathology, chronic liver disease or cancer biology; this is welcome but not required.

Being eligible to apply for a FWO PhD fellowship. See following link for criteria. https://www.fwo.be/en/support-programmes/phd-fellowships/#

Offer

A full-time PhD position for one year, extendable after a positive evaluation, with funding foreseen for a total of four years.

A multidisciplinary project with access to clinically relevant human datasets and expertise in pathology, molecular profiling, hepatology, oncology, radiology and AI.

Primary supervision by Prof. Olivier Govaere, in collaboration with Prof. Jeroen Dekervel and with co-supervision by Prof. Asier Antoranz.

Access to state-of-the-art computational and research infrastructure at KU Leuven.

Training in computational pathology, multimodal data integration, scientific communication and transferable skills through the KU Leuven doctoral programme.

Opportunities to collaborate with national and international research groups and present work at scientific meetings.

A challenging job as part of a small, dynamic and rapidly moving team performing cutting edge research at the forefront of translational science.

Remuneration according to the KU Leuven scholarships: https://www.kuleuven.be/personeel/jobsite/en/phd/phd-information#working-conditions

The PhD can begin as soon as possible, with flexibility in consultation with the supervisor.

Interested?

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Olivier Govaere, mail: [email protected] .

We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. 254042.body:
Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition.

Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences.  We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset.

Description of the research group
The Clinical Memory Research group at the Department of Clinical Sciences Malmö conducts leading research on biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative diseases, such as Lewy body dementia and Parkinson's disease. The research, internationally recognised through the BioFINDER studies, has for several years been at the forefront of fluid biomarkers and brain imaging, enabling early and accurate detection, diagnosis and prognosis of disease.
The group is led by Senior Lecturer Sebastian Palmqvist and Senior Lecturer Niklas Mattsson-Carlgren and consists of research staff and technical/administrative staff. The workplace is located at the Biomedical Centre (BMC) in Lund.
We work closely with the Memory Clinic at Skåne University Hospital in Malmö, where several of our researchers also work clinically. Read more about our research here
We are an international research group that values a good working environment characterised by respect and consideration. We strive for a workplace that is developing and stimulating for all employees, and we work continuously to create conditions that promote well-being, development and participation. We safeguard both physical safety and the psychosocial work environment.

What we offer
Lund University is a public authority, which means that you will have special benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension. We also have a flexitime agreement that creates good conditions for work/life balance.

Read more on the University’s website about being a Lund University employee, Work at Lund University
Project Description
The position is primarily associated with a five-year multicentre project (2026-2031) funded by the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) through a U01 grant for the clinical validation of the blood biomarker MTBR-tau243 in Alzheimer's disease, conducted in collaboration with Washington University in St. Louis , the University of Pennsylvania , and the University of Alabama at Birmingham . However, the work will encompass the activities of the entire research group and involve longitudinal data from several thousand participants in the BioFINDER studies , including blood and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, PET and MRI imaging, cognitive assessments, genetics, and proteomics.
Work duties and areas of responsibility
As biostatistician you work closely with the group's researchers and serve as a resource for statistical analysis. The primary task is to plan and carry out statistical analyses for scientific papers and to compile data across projects. The duties include: planning and carrying out statistical analyses for scientific publications together with the group's researchers, for example regarding diagnostic accuracy (ROC analysis, cutoffs, calibration, prediction models) and longitudinal data (mixed models, time-to-event, etc.)
compiling and quality-controlling analysis datasets from the group's databases across projects
producing clear, publication-quality figures and tables from the data
writing reproducible, well-documented analysis code in R
contributing to the U01 project's statistical analysis plan and pre-specified analyses, together with the Principal Investigator and statisticians at the US partner sites
drafting methods and results sections and reviewing the statistical parts of manuscripts
providing statistical advice on study design, power calculations and choice of methods
following methodological developments in the field and introducing new tools and ways of working in the group.

Qualifications
Requirements for the position:
a PhD in statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology or another relevant field with a clear statistical focus. The PhD must have been awarded by the time the employment decision is made.
excellent command of R, including data handling and programming of reproducible analyses.
a strong ability to visualise data and produce clear, publication-quality figures.
good knowledge of statistical modelling, in particular regression models, methods for diagnostic accuracy and analysis of longitudinal data.
excellent command of English, spoken and written (English is the group's working language).
great importance will be attached to personal qualities. We are looking for someone who is meticulous and structured, able to explain statistical methods and results to clinicians and researchers, service-minded and able to handle several parallel projects and deadlines.

Additional merits for the position:
previous experience of statistical analysis of clinical or medical data, in particular in biomarker, cohort or dementia research. This is a strong merit.
knowledge of our research field: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD).
co-authorship of scientific publications and experience of writing methods and results sections or other supporting text in manuscripts.
experience of writing statistical analysis plans and carrying out pre-specified analyses, for example in clinical trials or diagnostic validation studies.
experience of using LLM-based AI tools in statistical work (coding, documentation, drafting) and/or experience of machine learning on clinical data.
experience of data management in databases (e.g. REDCap, SQL) and harmonisation of variables across cohorts.
knowledge of Python or other programming languages.

Other information
This is a permanent position, 100 %, starting as soon as possible or according to agreement. A six months probationary period may be applied. Employment at Lund University is based in Sweden and you are therefore expected to carry out your work on site in Lund. Knowledge of Swedish is not a requirement for the position. The working language of the project is English
How to apply
Applications are made via the University's recruitment system. The application must include a cover letter describing how you meet the qualification requirements and why you are interested in the position, as well as a CV, degree certificate and any other documents you wish to refer to (copies of grades, contact details for references, letters of recommendation, etc.). The University applies individual salary setting; please state your salary expectation in your application.
The Faculty of Medicine is a part of Lund University, and is responsible for education and research within medicine and healthcare. Our academic programs are closely linked with the healthcare system and are firmly anchored in the faculty’s strong research tradition. Our research spans a broad field within experimental preclinical research, near-patient clinical research and health sciences research. The Faculty of Medicine, with its 1,800 employees and 2,700 students in Lund and Malmö, is a knowledge-intensive meeting place for students, teachers and researchers from all over the world.
The Department of Clinical Sciences, Malmö is one of the six departments at the Faculty of Medicine, Lund University. We have a strong focus on clinical and epidemiological research and also conduct an extensive preclinical laboratory research.
