Lunds universitet grundades 1666 och rankas återkommande som ett av världens främsta lärosäten. Här finns omkring 46 000 studenter och 8 500 medarbetare i Lund, Helsingborg och Malmö. Vi förenas i vår strävan att förstå, förklara och förbättra vår värld och människors villkor.

Lunds universitet välkomnar sökande med olika bakgrund och erfarenheter. Jämställdhet, lika villkor och mångfald är grundläggande principer för alla delar av vår verksamhet.
Beskrivning av forskargruppen
Forskargruppen Clinical Memory Research vid Institutionen för kliniska vetenskaper Malmö bedriver ledande forskning om biomarkörer för Alzheimers sjukdom och andra neurodegenerativa sjukdomar, såsom Lewykroppsdemens och Parkinsons sjukdom. Forskningen, som har fått internationellt erkännande genom BioFINDER-projekten, har under flera år legat i framkant inom området vätskebaserade biomarkörer och hjärnavbildning, vilket möjliggör tidig och korrekt upptäckt, diagnostik och prognos av sjukdom.
Gruppen leds av universitetslektor Sebastian Palmqvist och universitetslektor Niklas Mattsson-Carlgren och består av forsknings- samt teknisk/administrativ personal. Arbetsplatsen är belägen vid Biomedicinskt centrum (BMC) i Lund.
Vi samarbetar nära med Minnesmottagningen vid Skånes universitetssjukhus i Malmö, där flera av våra forskare även arbetar kliniskt. Du kan läsa mer om vår spännande forskning här
Vi är en internationell forskargrupp som värdesätter en god arbetsmiljö präglad av respekt och omtanke i våra möten. Vi eftersträvar en arbetsplats som upplevs som utvecklande och stimulerande för alla medarbetare. Vi arbetar kontinuerligt med att skapa förutsättningar som främjar trivsel, utveckling och delaktighet. Vi värnar om både den fysiska säkerheten och den psykosociala arbetsmiljön.
Vi erbjuder
Lunds universitet är en statlig myndighet vilket innebär att du får särskilda förmåner, generös semester och en förmånlig tjänstepension. Vi har även ett flextidsavtal som skapar goda förutsättningar för balans mellan arbete och fritid.

Läs mer på universitetets webbplats om att vara anställd vid Lunds universitet  Jobba hos oss
Projektbeskrivning
Anställningen är i första hand knuten till ett femårigt multicenterprojekt (2026–2031) som finansieras av amerikanska National Institutes of Health (NIH) genom ett så kallat U01-anslag, för klinisk validering av blodbiomarkören MTBR-tau243 vid Alzheimers sjukdom tillsammans med Washington University in St. Louis, University of Pennsylvania och University of Alabama at Birmingham. Arbetet omfattar dock hela forskargruppens verksamhet, med longitudinella data från flera tusen deltagare i BioFINDER-studierna (biomarkörer i blod och ryggvätska, PET- och MR-avbildning, kognition, genetik och proteomik).
Arbetsuppgifter och ansvarsområden
Som biostatistiker arbetar du nära gruppens forskare och utgör en resurs för statistisk analys. Den primära uppgiften är att planera och genomföra statistiska analyser till vetenskapliga artiklar och att sammanställa data i olika projekt. Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar bland annat att:
planera och genomföra statistiska analyser till vetenskapliga publikationer i samarbete med gruppens forskare, t.ex. avseende diagnostisk precision (ROC-analys, cutoffs, kalibrering, prediktionsmodeller) och longitudinella data (mixed models, tid till händelse m.m.)
sammanställa och kvalitetssäkra analysdataset från gruppens databaser i olika projekt
ta fram tydliga figurer och tabeller av publikationskvalitet utifrån data
skriva reproducerbar och väldokumenterad analyskod i R
bidra till U01-projektets statistiska analysplan och förspecificerade analyser, i samarbete med projektledaren och statistiker vid de amerikanska parterna
skriva utkast till metod- och resultatavsnitt samt granska statistiska delar av manus
ge statistisk rådgivning vid studiedesign, powerberäkningar och val av metod
följa metodutvecklingen inom området och introducera nya verktyg och arbetssätt i gruppen.

Kvalifikationer
För anställningen krävs.
doktorsexamen i statistik, biostatistik, epidemiologi eller annat relevant område med tydlig statistisk inriktning. Doktorsexamen ska vara avlagd senast vid tidpunkten då anställningsbeslut fattas.
mycket goda kunskaper i R, inklusive datahantering och programmering av reproducerbara analyser.
mycket god förmåga att visualisera data och skapa tydliga figurer av publikationskvalitet.
goda kunskaper i statistisk modellering, framför allt regressionsmodeller, metoder för diagnostisk precision och analys av longitudinella data.
mycket goda kunskaper i engelska i tal och skrift (engelska är gruppens arbetsspråk).
stor vikt kommer att läggas vid personliga egenskaper. Den vi söker är noggrann och strukturerad, har god förmåga att förklara statistiska metoder och resultat för kliniker och forskare, är serviceinriktad och kan arbeta med flera parallella projekt och deadlines.

Meriterande för anställningen är:
tidigare erfarenhet av statistiska analyser av kliniska eller medicinska data, särskilt inom biomarkör-, kohort- eller demensforskning. Detta är mycket meriterande.
kunskap inom vårt forskningsfält: Alzheimers sjukdom och andra neurodegenerativa sjukdomar (AD/ADRD).
medförfattarskap på vetenskapliga publikationer och vana att skriva metod- och resultatavsnitt eller andra stödjande textavsnitt i manus.
erfarenhet av att skriva statistiska analysplaner och genomföra förspecificerade analyser, t.ex. inom kliniska prövningar eller diagnostiska valideringsstudier.
vana att använda LLM-baserade AI-verktyg i statistiskt arbete (kodning, dokumentation, textutkast) och/eller erfarenhet av maskininlärning på kliniska data.
erfarenhet av datahantering i databaser (t.ex. REDCap, SQL) och harmonisering av variabler mellan kohorter.
kunskaper i Python eller andra programmeringsspråk.

Övrigt
Anställningen är en tillsvidareanställning med omfattning 100 % och tillträde snarast, enligt överenskommelse. Provanställning i sex månader kan komma att tillämpas. Anställningar vid Lunds universitet bedrivs i Sverige, du förväntas därför kunna utföra ditt arbete på plats i Lund.
Kunskaper i svenska är inte ett krav för anställningen. Projektets arbetsspråk är engelska.
Så här söker du
Anställningen söks via universitetets rekryteringssystem. Ansökan ska innehålla ett personligt brev där du beskriver hur du uppfyller kvalifikationskraven samt varför du är intresserad av anställningen. Ansökan ska även innehålla CV, examensbevis samt övrigt som du önskar åberopa (kopior av betyg, uppgifter till referenser, rekommendationsbrev etc.). Universitetet tillämpar individuell lönesättning. Ange gärna löneanspråk i din ansökan.
Universitetet tillämpar individuell lönesättning. Ange gärna löneanspråk i din ansökan.
Medicinska fakulteten är ett verksamhetsområde inom Lunds universitet, med ansvar för utbildning och forskning inom medicin, vård och hälsa. Utbildningen sker i nära samverkan med sjukvården och är väl förankrad i fakultetens starka forskningstradition. Fakultetens forskning spänner över ett brett fält inom experimentell grundforskning, patientnära klinisk forskning och hälsovetenskaplig forskning. Medicinska fakulteten, med drygt 1800 anställda och 3000 studenter i Lund, Malmö och Helsingborg, är en kunskapsintensiv mötesplats för studenter, lärare och forskare från hela världen.
Institutionen för kliniska vetenskaper i Malmö är en av de sex institutionerna vid Lunds universitets medicinska fakultet. Vi har ett starkt fokus på klinisk och epidemiologisk forskning, och bedriver även en omfattande preklinisk laboratorieforskning.
Vi undanber oss alla kontakter från annonsförsäljare, rekryterings- och bemanningsföretag på grund av statliga upphandlingsregler.

254058.body:
Can a battery cathode be made from phosphorus recovered from municipal wastewater? Join us at Chalmers University of Technology to investigate how recovered phosphorus can be converted into battery-grade lithium iron phosphate (LFP), working hands-on along the entire chain from waste-derived powder to tested battery cells.
About us
You will join Daniel Weber’s research group at the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering , with co-supervision from Martina Petranikova’s hydrometallurgy group within the same department. You will work alongside doctoral students and postdocs with experience from previous research projects, providing a collaborative environment for developing your experimental skills.
Our research facilities include furnaces with various atmospheres, stirred tank reactors and a spray dryer for precursor synthesis, an Ar glovebox, PXRD (housed at Chalmers Materials Analysis Laboratory ), TGA-DSC, Raman and IR spectroscopy, ICP and XRF, a laser diffraction particle size analyzer, and a battery assembly line with cell testing equipment.
Large-format pouch cells of the most promising materials will be built and tested in collaboration with a partner university in Germany. Through the project's industrial advisory board and potential research stay, you will have opportunities to engage directly with industrial partners and gain insight into how your research results can be applied in practice.
About the research project
The PHOS4CELL project investigates whether phosphorus recovered from municipal wastewater can be converted into battery-grade lithium iron phosphate (LFP). You will study how impurities in recovered phosphorus affect battery capacity and cycle life, which contaminants can be tolerated and which must be removed. By synthesizing, characterizing and testing LFP from different phosphorus sources, you will explore how recycled materials can contribute to a more sustainable battery value chain.
The four-year project is funded by the Swedish Energy Agency within the program Sustainable battery value chain (Hållbar batterivärdekedja). It brings together researchers from Chalmers, Polestar and industrial partners across the LFP value chain. The project may also include a research stay at a European LFP cathode producer.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master's degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy or a closely related field.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Documented hands-on experience from a materials chemistry laboratory, including inorganic powder synthesis, and/or hydrometallurgical processing of materials.
Ability to independently plan and conduct laboratory experiments, identify and resolve experimental problems, and maintain accurate and systematic documentation of results.
Good communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to work with researchers and engineers from different disciplines and industrial partners.
A curious and analytical approach to experimental research, with a willingness to investigate and understand unexpected results.

The following experience will strengthen your application:
Solid-state or wet-chemical synthesis of inorganic functional materials, particularly phosphates, iron compounds or battery cathode materials.
Experience with reduction of Fe(III) under hydrogen or carbothermal conditions.
Powder X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement (e.g. TOPAS, GSAS-II or FullProf), including quantitative phase analysis.
Experience controlling particle size and morphology through precipitation, milling, spray drying or similar methods.
Proficiency in Swedish, as the project involves regular interaction with Swedish industrial partners.
Experience working with or for industry, or in research projects involving industrial partners.
Familiarity with Matlab, Python or similar programming languages for data analysis and visualization, and with statistical or data-driven experimental design.

What you will do
Synthesize LFP cathode materials from waste-derived phosphorus and commercial reference reagents, incl. calcination, milling, reduction under hydrogen or carbothermal conditions, and carbon coating.
Purify and characterize secondary phosphorus feedstocks and intermediates using hydrometallurgical methods, in collaboration with the Petranikova group, and quantify impurities using techniques such as XRF, ICP, TOC and CHNS analysis.
Characterize material structure, composition and morphology using powder X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement, particle size analysis, electron microscopy and thermal analysis.
Investigate particle engineering through precipitation and spray drying to achieve particle sizes and tap densities relevant to industrial applications.
Assemble and test half and full coin cells, and relate their electrochemical performance to material composition, impurity profiles and particle properties.
Take courses at an advanced level within the relevant graduate school at Chalmers. Read more about our graduate schools .
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing.
The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.
Collaborate with industrial partners through advisory board meetings, sample exchanges and discussions of technical specifications, with the possibility of an industrial research stay.
Publish research results in peer-reviewed journals, present findings at national and international conferences, and contribute to the supervision of bachelor's and master's students.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about working at Chalmers and our benefits for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden's generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc. at Move To Gothenburg .

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence .
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.

Do you want to contribute to impactful research in the data-driven Food and Health field?   Join our team as a Doctoral student at the Division of Food and Nutrition Science, Department of Life Sciences.
About us
The Department of Life Sciences conducts research, innovation, and education to enable a biobased society and improve human health. We explore how biological systems, and innovative technologies can be used to convert biomass into valuable products. We use advanced computational technologies to discover how biomolecules and organisms function and interact. We pioneer new methods for prediction, prevention, diagnostics and treatment of diseases.
The Division of Food and Nutrition Science addresses major societal challenges related to sustainable food production, nutrition and health. We conduct research, innovation, education and dissemination with the aim to provide new knowledge and solutions for a sustainable planet and healthy humans.
About the research project
This doctoral position is an opportunity to work at the intersection of nutrition, multi-omics, and precision health in a strong technical and natural sciences environment well connected with clinial enviromnets in Gothenburg and internationlly. You will join a dynamic, international academic community that values scientific excellence, innovation, and sustainable development. The role is designed for a curious, skilled and motivated person who wants to build a research career and contribute to better understanding how nutrition shapes human health at a molecular level.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in chemometry, bioinformatics, food and nutrition science, biotechnology, engineering or similar
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Experience in computational metabolomics and microbiome research

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience in large scale OMICs-data handling and statistical analysis
Documented programming skills and excellent R user.
Previous experience from scientific data generation, analysis and publishing
Hands on skills in metabolomics and multi-modal data integration

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Bioscience  ( Bioscience | Chalmers  )
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing
The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours
Data management and programming support to other graduate students in the environment.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.

Institute of Biomedicine is looking for a University Teacher for a fixed term position which focuses on the following teaching areas: bioimaging informatics, artificial intelligence and machine learning based (image) data analysis. The position will be filled from 1 January 2027 onwards (or as agreed) for three years.
Job description
The position of a university teacher includes a wide range of teaching duties within the degree programmes in biomedical sciences, medicine and dentistry. Teaching duties and course responsibilities are primarily within undergraduate education, including our international Master’s programmes (the Master’s programme in Bioimaging and the Master’s programme in Drug Discovery and Development). Teaching duties include, amongst other things, the planning and conducting of lectures, examinations, practical assignments and online teaching. Teaching may be conducted in both Finnish and English. The role also includes supervising theses, tasks related to the organisation, planning and development of teaching, high-level research work, and university administrative duties. The successful candidate will be expected to participate actively in research in the field and to apply for research funding.  Read more about studying at the Faculty of Medicine .
Who we are looking for
According to the qualification requirements, a person selected for the post of a university teacher is must have
an applicable higher university degree
good teaching skills

When assessing the merits of the applicants, the following will be taken into account
the teaching and research expertise within the relevant field
teacher training
the ability to produce study materials and multifaceted teaching
recent publications in the field as well as other academic merits

To succeed in this role, you will need
experience of modern machine learning methods
an understanding of deep neural networks
programming skills, particularly in the Python programming language and relevant development environments
experience of biomedical imaging
an enthusiastic and innovative approach to teaching
the ability to supervise international students
excellent spoken and written English
strong teamwork skills in a multidisciplinary and multicultural environment
good organisational skills and the ability to work under pressure (time management, managing multiple tasks simultaneously)
the ability to deliver multifaceted teaching and develop digital learning environments

The eligibility criteria for the position must be met by the end of the application period.
The following may be considered as an advantage
a doctoral degree in a relevant field
previous experience of publishing, teaching and supervising in the field
a proven track record of securing research funding
international research experience
experience of high-performance computing or parallel computing environments
proficiency in Finnish
a vision for the direction of research in this role
familiarity with the degree programmes offered by the University of Turku and the Faculty of Medicine
practical experience of teaching/teaching responsibilities and research in the field of biomedicine
compatibility of the candidate’s own research topics with the research priorities of the Institute of Biomedicine

We value collegiality and promote equality, diversity, and inclusivity. We encourage all qualified applicants with different backgrounds to apply for our open positions.
Benefits
We offer you responsible and interesting tasks and the opportunity to develop your professional skills in a versatile operating environment. Please read more about University of Turku as an employer from our  Come work with us!  pages.
The European Commission has awarded the University of Turku the right to use the  HR Excellence in Research quality label . The label is a token of the University's commitment to continuous development of the position and working conditions of researchers according to the guidelines set forth in the European Charter for Researchers.
The University of Turku has several high-quality research infrastructures required for cutting-edge research. Learn more about the roadmap of research infrastructures and how the research infrastructure and expert teams offer tailored solutions for businesses and organizations .
The University of Turku is among the top of the world’s universities in most rankings and among the best universities in the world in certain fields. Our high-quality basic research, a multidisciplinary research profile and close cooperation in research infrastructures creates the basis for international top research. Read more about University of Turku in international university rankings.
The university offers good support and orientation for international hires. Please learn more about the Finnish culture and relocation to Finland:
City of Turku
Welcome visitor
International House of Turku
Working culture:  infoFinland.fi
This is Finland
Careers in Southwest Finland
Finland - a superpower of education and innovations | University of Turku (utu.fi)

Salary and trial period
The salary is determined in accordance with the university salary system for teaching and research personnel (levels 4-6). In addition, a personal performance-based salary component is paid. At the beginning of the employment, the gross monthly salary is typically approximately EUR 3197-4671, depending on previous experience and expertise. The amount of the salary is defined when the employment contract is prepared. A six (6) month trial period applies to the position.
How to apply
Please submit your application through our online recruitment system by 4 November 2026 4 pm.
Applications should include:
CV ( use this template )
list of publications
motivation letter
teaching portfolio in accordance with the University guidelines
copy of a degree certificate
contact information of two referees
other relevant documents

Additional information
For further information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Pekka Ruusuvuori, [email protected]
In case you need help with the application process, please turn to HR Specialist Kristiina Nuutila, [email protected] , +358 50 313 5224

Institute of Biomedicine

Research at the Institute of Biomedicine is divided into three functional units: Infection and Immunity, Integrative Physiology and Pharmacology, and Cancer research. Research at our Institute includes both biomedical basic research and translational research, and the unit division expresses our research priorities.
The Faculty of Medicine is a high level, international and innovative research and education unit in biomedicine, clinical medicine, dentistry and health and nursing sciences, as well as a major social contributor to health promotion, disease genesis, in the research of diagnostics and treatment and in the development of the health service and education system. The faculty provides research-based multidisciplinary undergraduate education in educational programs that educate diverse and critically minded specialists. The research is multidisciplinary and results in new information aimed at promoting the health of the population and better patient care.
The University of Turku is an inspiring and international academic community of 25,000 students and staff in Southwest Finland. We build a sustainable future with multidisciplinary research, education, and collaboration. With us, your work will have a significant impact and relevance in the changing world.
See our open vacancies

Information for the applicant
The application form cannot be saved as a draft. However, after submitting you can return to edit your application via the link you receive by email. The application can be edited until the application deadline.
You have 6 hours to complete your application before the timeout.

Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research?
As a research assistant, you will join the Perception Lab at the Department of Clinical Neuroscience, Karolinska Institutet. The group studies the neural basis of the human sense of smell using psychophysics, functional neuroimaging and electrophysiology. In this role, you will contribute to data collection in ongoing studies, with a focus on conducting EEG testing to understand how the human brain processes odours.
Your mission
You will do research in ongoing studies. Your tasks include conducting EEG testing and standardised olfactory psychophysical tests with research participants, assisting in the preparation and execution of neuroimaging (MRI) studies, and contributing to data management, documentation and the practical coordination of test sessions.
Your profile
To be eligible for employment as a research assistant, you must hold a bachelor’s degree in a subject that we consider relevant to the position. Fluency in spoken and written English is required. You are well-organized, meticulous, and able to work independently as well as in a team. As you will be in direct contact with research participants and patients, a high level of social and communication skills is required. Great emphasis will be placed on personal suitability.
Documented experience in the following is a strong advantage :
EEG recordings
EEG analysis
Programming in MATLAB and/or Python
Olfactory psychophysical testing
Working in a research environment (e.g. as a research assistant)

It is also an advantage if you have:
MR safety certification and experience operating an MRI scanner
Very good knowledge of Swedish

What do we offer?
A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is also a state university, which entitles you to several good benefits through our collective agreement. And you get to practice freely in our modern wellness facilities, where trained staff are on site.
Location: Solna

254165.body:
Introduction
Data centers are the backbone of the digital economy, but their exponential growth in energy consumption-driven by AI and machine learning workloads-demands transformative solutions. The next-generation of data centers will be based on Solid-State Transformer, which enables energy distribution with higher efficiency, grid-friendly data center operation and etc.
This PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of power electronics, control systems, and grid integration, with direct collaboration with Delta Energy System GmbH, a global leader in power conversion for data centers. Your research will focus on power electronics converters for SST, focusing on the DC-DC stage.
Job Description
As a PhD candidate in the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group at TU/e, you will with solid-state transformers (SST) for datacenter, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Your research will address the critical challenges of power density, efficiency, and grid stability in modern data centers, focusing on the converter design and advanced control/modulation strategies to achieve high performance and high controllability. Additionally, the design should be validate with experimental results. Your work will directly contribute to the sustainability of AI infrastructure by enabling data centers to efficiently integrate renewable energy sources, support grid stability, and reduce their carbon footprint. With access to cutting-edge tools and industrial collaboration, you will have the opportunity to shape the future of power electronics for data centers.
Job Requirements
A master's degree (or equivalent university degree) in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Control Systems, or a related field.
A research-oriented attitude with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interest in collaborating with industrial partners.
Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.

Based on our candidate assessment, the following skills are valuable:
Required:
Demonstrated knowledge in power converter topologies (e.g., DC-DC, AC-DC, multilevel converters).
Familiarity with control theory (e.g., classical control, state-space methods, model predictive control).
Experience with simulation tools (MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, or similar).
Understanding of grid integration challenges (e.g., power quality, stability, renewable energy interfacing).

Advantageous:
Hands-on experience with prototyping and experimental validation of power converters.
Affinity with embedded systems (DSP, FPGA) for real-time control implementation.

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process .

Introduction
Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing.
Job Description
Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. While housing upgrades are often motivated by sustainability and affordability goals, we focus on their potential benefits for future generations. How does inadequate housing during pregnancy and early childhood affect children's health and development? Which housing upgrades offer the greatest benefits? And how can behavioural modelling, big data and AI help shape healthier, more equitable homes? These are the questions your PhD research will tackle.
You will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers and practitioners, working at the intersection of housing, public health, climate adaptation, and social equity. Combining medical and behavioural insights, large-scale data analysis, computer vision and advanced statistical methods, you will be tranforming complex unstructured housing and health data into predictive models. The results will feed into a digital tool to predict and optimise the impact of housing upgrades across different scenarios, helping housing providers and municipalities create healthier, more resilient homes for families.
This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners.
As a PhD candidate, you will be part of the TU/e's internationally renowned Urban Systems and Real Estate group (Department of the Built Environment), conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of urban systems, real estate, data science, and smart technologies. The four-year program combines advanced training with impactful research, offering strong support for professional development through courses, seminars, and international conferences. You will collaborate closely with scientific partners at Erasmus Medical Centre, Erasmus University Rotterdam, VU University Amsterdam, as well as societal partners including housing providers, municipalities and engineering bureaus.

An MSc degree in Exact or data sciences/ Quantitative economics/ Engineering.

254170.body:
When the Mundane Becomes Transformational. Everyday self-provisioning practices as form of prefiguration for a degrowth future

The PhD research examines the transformative potential of alternative self-provision practices (e.g. food self-provisioning, sharing, repair and DIY) as pathways to degrowth. It explores how everyday practices can be system-changing (e.g. prefiguration, prosumption, quiet sustainability) and under what conditions they support economic transformation “from below”, drawing on qualitative research on alternative/ecological economies, degrowth and sustainability.

The project will address the following key areas:
While alternative self-provision practices, incl. food self-provisioning, foraging, informal sharing economy practices, repair and DIY, have hitherto remained largely invisible in mainstream economic thinking (Pungas 2023), they have recently gained increasing attention in the research on quiet sustainability (Smith and Jehlicka 2013, Sovova et al. 2025), prefiguration (Siddharth et al. 2026) and degrowth (Spanier et al. 2024). Yet evidence on whether and under what conditions such seemingly mundane everyday practices can contribute to transformative change remains fragmented (cf Forno and Wahlen 2022). Some research has questioned their political and transformative potential (e.g. Goodman et al. 2012), while other studies have highlighted pathways from individual practices towards collective forms of action, such as local food solidarity networks and community-based FSP initiatives (Forno et al, 2015; Guidi and Andretta, 2015; Smith and Jehlicka 2013, Sovova et al. 2025). Tapping into this gap, this PhD project sets out to explore the transformative potential of alternative self-provision practices for a degrowth future .
The thesis should address questions such as:
If and how can mundane and quiet practices be seen as part of a degrowth future or “nowtopia”? Do practitioners see them as such, why/why not? (in other words, is a prefigurative mindset needed for prefigurative change)
Which practices and quiet sustainability niches exist in Estonia, how do they emerge and which are their development paths?
What are the motives, barriers / enablers and potential pathways from seemingly mundane everyday self-provisioning practices toward broader economic and business transformation (e.g. degrowth and sustainability management, doughnut, diverse, degrowth economies)? (in other words, systemic scaling of quiet small-scale practices)

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
The selected PhD candidate will be granted independence regarding the choice of theoretical framing, research philosophy, and methodological emphasis, while working within the broader framework outlined above. The project is expected to involve mixed-method qualitative research. The PhD candidate should already have learned, or be willing to learn, one or more research methodologies and methods such as qualitative interviewing, case-study analysis, participatory observation and fieldwork, as well as qualitative research analysis.
The PhD candidate’s work is expected to engage with several empirical components, including:
Mapping of existing mundane self-provisioning practices in Estonia , and former research studying these (e.g. foraging, dacha gardening, informal food (exchange) networks, organic non-profit farms/semi-self-sufficiency farms, repair, DIY)
Multiple case studies with self-provisioning practitioners to understand their pathways, practices, networks and relation to the conventional (market-based) system and transformative impact/intention
Exploration with self-provision practitioners and dis-/enabling system stake-holders about the possible pathways from prefiguration to system change
Analysis of findings from a system transformation / degrowth (or other suitable alternative economy and management) perspective

The candidate’s main task will be to prepare a doctoral thesis under the supervision of Ass. Prof. Bianka Plüschke-Altof. The candidate is also expected to engage in small-scale teaching, contribute to topic-related project proposals, and actively participate in the department’s academic life.

The candidate is expected to have:
a master’s degree in social sciences (e.g. sociology, human geography, economics), management, anthropology, or a related field
a clear interest in the topic
excellent command of English and Estonian
strong and demonstrable writing and analytical skills
capacity to work both as an independent researcher and part of a research team
capacity and willingness to contribute to teaching and organisational tasks

The candidate must submit a research plan (5 pages) for the topic , including a preliminary overview of relevant literature and an overall research design. The candidate may expand on the listed research questions and tasks and propose specific theoretical lenses and methods to be used.

The following experience is beneficial:
working knowledge of qualitative research methods
familiarity with mixed-method designs or willingness to learn
knowledge of topics such as prefiguration, quiet sustainability, alternative economic practices, system transformation, degrowth
experience in fieldwork and participatory research

About the Project
PhD Position: Control Capacity of Active Matter Using Activity Landscapes
The Molecular Nanophotonics Group at Leipzig University, led by Prof. Dr. Frank Cichos, invites applications for a doctoral researcher position in a joint ISF-DFG project with the group of Prof. Dr. Yael Roichman at Tel Aviv University. Our group pioneered “photon nudging”, the feedback control of light-driven microswimmers, and has since combined it with reinforcement learning, physical reservoir computing and programmable hydrodynamics.
Start Date: January 1, 2027 (or earliest possible date)
Research Focus: How many collective degrees of freedom of an active system can we actually control, and at what energetic cost? You will help to build a quantitative framework for controlling active matter with light, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and control theory. The project combines:
Self-thermophoretic Janus microswimmers driven by dynamic laser landscapes (Cichos group, Leipzig)
Light-powered bristle robots on a programmable LED arena (Roichman group, Tel Aviv University)
A shared theoretical framework built on fundamental thermodynamic limits

Comparing microswimmers with robots will reveal which limits of control are universal, from single particles to swarms, with applications from microswimmer transport to energy-efficient swarm robotics.
What You Will Do
Design and run experiments with light-driven Janus microswimmers, shaping activity landscapes in real time with a spatial light modulator
Fabricate microfluidic chips and measure the energy that drives the particles
Track hundreds of interacting particles with machine-learning methods and test fundamental thermodynamic bounds on control
Work closely with the Tel Aviv team through monthly joint meetings
Present findings at international conferences and co-author publications in high-impact journals

Qualifications
Master's degree in Physics or Physical Chemistry with excellent academic standing
Solid background in soft matter, statistical or non-equilibrium physics, and a keen interest in connecting experiment with theory
Hands-on experience in optics, video microscopy, particle tracking and/or microfluidics
Programming experience for data analysis and experiment automation (Python preferred; machine-learning experience is a plus)
Excellent English and enjoyment of interdisciplinary teamwork

What We Offer
State-of-the-art laser and microscopy setups for real-time, light-driven control of active particles
Research stays in the Roichman lab in Tel Aviv and a binational team working on shared protocols and joint publications
The chance to help shape a new research direction at the interface of active matter, stochastic thermodynamics and control
Support for international conference travel
Professional development opportunities including teaching experience and transferable skills training
Vibrant research community in a culturally rich and affordable European city

Application Process
Please submit the following documents and information to [email protected]   by 16 November 2026:
Cover letter (max. 1 page) outlining your interest in the project, relevant skills and career goals
CV/resume including any publications or conference presentations
Academic transcripts (bachelor’s and master’s degrees)
Names and contact information of at least two academic references

About Leipzig University
Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany's leading research institutions with a strong international focus.
For more information about our research:  https://www.uni-leipzig.de/~mona Partner group in Tel Aviv:   https://www.roichmanlab.sites.tau.ac.il/
We are committed to increasing diversity in STEM and strongly encourage applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds.

Do you want to help create the next generation of sustainable 3D products from pulp fibres? In this Doctoral project, you will combine materials science, mechanics and multiscale characterisation to establish predictive design rules for transforming fibres into advanced products. You will contribute to research with the potential to replace fossil-based plastics with sustainable alternatives.
About us
The Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering pushes the knowledge of chemistry and chemical engineering forward in a broad field of research and education. We offer an international environment, with scientific areas ranging from fundamental chemistry, health and medical technology, materials science, renewable energy, to chemical engineering processing, material recycling, nuclear chemistry, theory and modelling.
The Division of Applied Chemistry
We primarily focus on applied research, that is, research aimed at addressing societal challenges and that is ready for implementation either immediately or in the near future. Examples of application areas include fossil-free fuels and energy systems, electronic devices, health and technology, the utilisation of fibres and forest-based materials, and various forms of catalysis.
About the research project
Can pulp fibres be engineered into complex 3D products that rival conventional plastics?
This Doctoral project aims to transform fibre-based manufacturing from trial-and-error development to predictive design. You will combine experiments, mechanical analysis and multiscale material characterisation to uncover how fibre properties govern deformability, damage, spring-back and shape retention in 3D forming processes.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (120 credits) or an equivalent degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Fibre and Polymer Technology, Wood Technology, Engineering Physics, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology or a related field.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Documented experience from experimental research, thesis work, or industrial projects related to materials, mechanics, manufacturing, polymers, fibre-based materials, or modelling.
Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex experimental data
Ability to collaborate effectively and communicate clearly in multidisciplinary and international environments.

The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience with fibre-based materials, polymers, paper, packaging, or other sustainable material systems.
Experience in experimental materials characterisation, mechanical testing, microscopy, image analysis, or related analytical techniques.
Experience with data analysis, modelling, finite element methods, or programming (e.g. Python, MATLAB, or similar tools).
Experience working in interdisciplinary teams and communicating scientific results in written reports or presentations.

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Chalmers graduate education system and actively participate in the research environment of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a Vinnova Competence Centre bringing together academia and industry.
Conduct research aimed at understanding how fibre properties, material structure and processing conditions influence the formability of lignocellulosic materials into complex three-dimensional products. You will combine experimental studies, multiscale characterisation and data analysis to develop predictive design principles for fibre-based manufacturing.
Develop your own scientific ideas and communicate research results through publications in international journals, presentations at conferences, and interactions with industrial partners.
Collaborate with researchers from Chalmers, KTH and industrial partners within FibRe, contributing to the development of sustainable alternatives to fossil-based plastics.
The position generally includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or other departmental duties corresponding to up to 20% of full-time employment.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
The successful candidate will be employed by Chalmers University of Technology and enrolled in the doctoral education programme upon admission.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.
The doctoral student will be part of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a VINNOVA Competence Centre involving close collaboration with academic and industrial partners and Area of Advance Production .

As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.

254246.body:
Student Research Assistant in Bridge Monitoring, Computer Vision & Data Science
The Chair of Structural Mechanics & Monitoring , led by Prof. Eleni Chatzi, conducts research at the intersection of structural engineering, sensing, data science, and artificial intelligence for infrastructure monitoring.

We are looking for a Student Research Assistant with a background in structural engineering, signal processing, data science, computer vision, or related fields to support our ongoing SwissBWIM project. The project combines bridge structural monitoring and traffic monitoring data to identify vehicle loads and assess the structural condition and performance of highway bridges.

Project background
Our project, “SWISS-BWIM: Multi-functional bridge loads and condition assessment,” develops robust and cost-efficient methods for bridge load identification and condition assessment based on the Bridge Weigh-in-Motion (B-WIM) concept.

B-WIM uses sensors installed directly on bridges to estimate the loads of passing vehicles from the bridge response they induce. The same monitoring data can also provide information on structural behaviour and condition. By combining identified traffic loads with structural response, the project aims to derive performance indicators such as dynamic amplification factors, response envelopes, and load-response relationships, and ultimately support the identification of abnormal behaviour and potential damage.

We have completed monitoring-system installations on several highway bridges in Switzerland and are continuously collecting large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including bridge acceleration, strain and displacement measurements, environmental data, and traffic videos.

The Student Research Assistant will work with an analysis framework which has been developed by our Chair to process and integrate these datasets. Depending on background and interest, there will also be opportunities to develop and test new methods for traffic-load identification, computer-vision-based traffic monitoring, and structural health monitoring under the supervision of experienced researchers

Job description
The main tasks include:

Multi-modal data preprocessing: synchronising measurements from different sensing systems, identifying and cleaning faulty data, and improving data organisation and storage.

Traffic video analysis: applying deep-learning-based computer vision methods for vehicle detection and tracking; manually labelling data and fine-tuning models where needed; and using camera calibration and geometric transformation to determine vehicle locations and trajectories on the bridge.

Bridge Weigh-in-Motion analysis: fusing vehicle trajectories with bridge acceleration, strain and displacement measurements to estimate traffic loads.

Structural monitoring: analysing structural and environmental measurements to extract key performance indicators and investigate changes in bridge behaviour and structural condition.

Integrated condition assessment: combining identified traffic loads with structural response indicators to support more comprehensive assessment of bridge performance and condition.

Please note that the methods required to complete most of the tasks above have already been developed by our Chair. Depending on the candidate’s background and interests, there will also be opportunities to develop and test new methods.

Profile
We are looking for a motivated student who can contribute to several of the areas above. Ideally, you:

Are currently enrolled at a university in Zurich or the nearby area.

Have a background in civil/structural engineering, mechanical engineering, data science, computer science, or a related field.

Have experience or strong interest in two or more of the following:

bridge engineering, structural dynamics, or system identification;

sensing systems and signal processing;

data analysis and machine learning;

computer vision, particularly object detection, tracking, or localisation.

Are familiar with Python programming. Experience with MATLAB and Linux is an advantage.

Can dedicate 15 hours per week to the project.

Enjoy working on real-world engineering problems and developing practical, data-driven solutions.

Are proficient in English. The working language of our group is English.

Please note that you are not expected to have prior experience in all of the areas listed above . We particularly welcome applicants who have a strong foundation in two or more of them and are motivated to learn the others.

We offer

Salary in accordance with ETH Zurich’s standard rates for student assistants.

Access to sufficient computational resources, including CPU and GPU computing on Euler, ETH Zurich's high-performance computing cluster.

A workplace in our offices on the ETH Zurich Hönggerberg campus.

Hands-on experience with real-world bridge monitoring systems and large-scale multi-modal datasets.

Close supervision and the opportunity to work at the intersection of structural engineering, sensing, computer vision, and data science.

A collaborative and international research environment within the Chair of Structural Mechanics & Monitoring.

We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

254260.body:
About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine.
Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in.
We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the IAS Audacity project AI4TECS, which investigates how advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques can enable real‑time identification and treatment of emerging contaminants (ECs). AI4TECS aims to develop the first AI‑powered system that integrates real‑time EC identification using non-target high resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) data, toxicity prediction, and transformation modelling into an early‑warning monitoring framework.
Your role
Conducting excellent collaborative research within the project AI4TECS. The person will pursue three core research directions: Developing a foundation model capable of identifying ECs directly from complex LC‑HRMS data
Designing hierarchical graph‑based models to predict toxicity under uncertainty by linking molecular‑level and system‑level knowledge
Advancing causal inference methods to predict transformation products (TPs) under varying treatment conditions

Writing a doctoral dissertation in computer science
Publishing research findings in leading international conferences and high‑impact journals in AI, machine learning, and environmental sciences
Presenting results at scientific meetings, workshops, and project events, contributing to the visibility and impact of the AI4TECS project
Potential participation in teaching activities

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary project team with expertise spanning environmental chemistry, AI, and water‑treatment engineering. Collaboration is central to the project's design. Throughout the project, the candidate will work closely with a second doctoral researcher to be recruited within the Environmental Cheminformatics Group (ECI) at LCSB. The ECI PhD candidate will perform prioritized Non-Targeted Assessment (pNTA) across diverse water matrices and case studies, while the AI4Science PhD (this position) will develop machine‑learning models that learn from and build upon these pNTA results.

The successful candidate will be employed at the Department of Computer Science of the University of Luxembourg (UL) and have access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources suitable for large-scale machine-learning and foundation-model experiments. They will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jun Pang and Dr. Zhiqiang Zhong.

For further information about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Jun Pang and Dr. Zhiqiang Zhong (firstname.lastname_AT_uni.lu).
Your profile
A Master's degree in computer science or a closely related field
Solid background in AI, with particular interest or experience in foundation models, e.g., representation learning, large‑scale pretraining, and graph machine learning, e.g., GNNs, graph representation learning, hierarchical or probabilistic graph models
Strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities, with enthusiasm for developing novel computational methods
Excellent programming skills and familiarity with modern deep learning frameworks
Strong interest in interdisciplinary research, and the ability to engage meaningfully with collaborators from environmental chemistry and water‑treatment engineering
Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English is required

Academic Eligibility (Thesis) :
Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply

Arbetsuppgifter
Enheten för Kraft och värme vid Institutionen för energiteknik söker en forskningsingenjör som ska bedriva forskning inom de Vinnova-finansierade projekten ”Inverkan av INlopps-Distorsion på AEROdynamiska och AEROelastiska egenskaper hos ett axiellt kompressorsteg (INDIAERO)” och ”AI Supported Adaptive Manufacturing (AISAM)”.
Projekten behandlar två viktiga aspekter som påverkar den aerodynamiska och aeromekaniska prestandan hos fläkt- och kompressorblad i flygplansmotorer: skovelerosion och inloppsdistorsion. Framkantserosion kan medföra ökade aerodynamiska förluster och därmed ökad bränsleförbrukning. Samtidigt utsätts flygplansmotorer ofta för ojämna inflödesförhållanden till följd av inloppsgeometri och varierande flygförhållanden, vilket kan påverka både aerodynamisk prestanda och aeroelastisk stabilitet samt medföra risk för exempelvis fladder och högcykelutmattning.
Tillförlitliga metoder för att bedöma dessa effekter är fortfarande under utveckling och utgör ett aktivt internationellt forskningsområde. Tillgång till högkvalitativa experimentella data är en viktig förutsättning för utveckling och validering av sådana metoder.
Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar utveckling och konstruktion av experimentella uppställningar, genomförande av detaljerade aerodynamiska mätningar samt analys och jämförelse av experimentella och numeriska resultat. Tjänsten innebär nära samarbete med de industriella partnerna som deltar i projekten.
Utöver forskningsaktiviteterna kan tjänsten även innefatta undervisning och andra utbildningsrelaterade aktiviteter motsvarande upp till 10 % av arbetstiden.

254330.body:
Bepaal mee de toekomst – Universiteit Antwerpen
De Universiteit Antwerpen is een dynamische, toekomstgerichte Europese universiteit. We bieden vernieuwend academisch onderwijs aan meer dan 20000 studenten, verrichten baanbrekend wetenschappelijk onderzoek en spelen een belangrijke dienstverlenende rol in de maatschappij. We zijn een van de grootste, meest internationale en innovatieve werkgevers van de regio. Met meer dan 6000 medewerkers uit 100 verschillende landen bouwen we dagelijks aan de wereld van morgen. Door wetenschappelijk toponderzoek verleggen we grenzen en geven we de richting aan. De richting van de toekomst. En die kan jij mee bepalen.
Het Departement Bio-ingenieurswetenschappen van de Faculteit Wetenschappen zoekt een voltijdse  doctoraatsbursaal in het domein foto-elektrochemie, sensing en model-based environmental control
Functie
Je werkt actief aan de voorbereiding en verdediging van een doctoraal proefschrift in het domein van bio-ingenieurswetenschappen. Je stelt een onderzoeksplan en bijhorende onderzoeksmethoden op in samenspraak met je promotor(en) en onderneemt de nodige administratieve stappen voor een vlot doctoraatsproces.
Je voert het onderzoek efficiënt en naar gepaste standaard uit, eventueel in het buitenland, en dingt mee naar financiering voor algemene of specifieke kosten.
Je rapporteert de voortgang aan je promotor(en) en commissies en presenteert je onderzoek op wetenschappelijke congressen.
Je verdedigt je proefschrift openbaar en streeft naar publicatie in de wetenschappelijke pers.

Je publiceert wetenschappelijke artikelen die verband houden met het onderzoeksproject.
Je neemt een beperkt pakket van onderwijs- en onderzoeksondersteunende en dienstverlenende taken op voor het Departement Bio-ingenieurswetenschappen.
Je doet mee aan de competitie voor interne of externe predoctorale financiering.

Profiel
Je behaalde een masterdiploma in bio-ingenieurswetenschappen of gerelateerde ingenieurswetenschappen of exacte wetenschappen, of een masterdiploma in connectie met het onderzoek in het departement, of je behaalt het diploma uiterlijk op het moment van aanstelling.
Je kan uitstekende studieresultaten voorleggen.
Je hebt een uitgesproken belangstelling in een onderzoeksonderwerp gelinkt aan minstens één van de professoren bij A-PECS : Antwerp Engineering, photoelectrochemistry and sensing: Professoren: Sammy Verbruggen , Karolien De Wael , Siegfried Denys , Tom Tytgat
Onderzoeksdomeinen: Foto(-elektro)katalyse, foto(-elektro)chemie, plasmonics, bio-elektrochemie, sensoren, diagnostiek, Luchtzuivering, luchtkwaliteitsanalyse, reactor design, computationele fluid dynamica modelleren, thermisch comfort, stedelijk groen

Je bent een gedreven persoon die bereid is actief onderzoeksfinanciering aan te vragen voor een doctoraat onder begeleiding van een hoofdpromotor verbonden aan de onderzoeksgroep A-PECS (vb. FWO-aspirant strategisch basisonderzoek, FWO-aspirant fundamenteel onderzoek...).
Je onderwijscompetenties sluiten aan bij de onderwijsvisie van de Universiteit Antwerpen.
Je onderzoekskwaliteiten sluiten aan bij het facultaire en universitaire onderzoeksbeleid en het Departement Bio-ingenieurswetenschappen.
Je bent communicatief en beheerst de Engelse taal.
Je gaat kwaliteitsgericht, integer, creatief en samenwerkingsgericht te werk.

Aanbod
We bieden een doctoraatsbeurs voor een periode van maximum één jaar.
We bieden de mogelijkheid om binnen het kader van je werkzaamheden deel te nemen aan wetenschappelijke activiteiten alsook de mogelijkheid om je verder te ontwikkelen via vorming en opleiding.
De voorziene startdatum is 1 januari 2027.
Je maandelijkse beurs wordt berekend volgens de beursbedragen voor doctoraatsbursalen in de barema’s voor het Bijzonder Academisch Personeel.
Je krijgt als doctoraatsonderzoeker toegang tot een breed en gevarieerd opleidingsaanbod en opleidingskrediet via de Antwerp Doctoral School .
Een open en flexibele werkomgeving die creativiteit, zelfontplooiing en zelfstandig denken stimuleert. Het team is dynamisch, respectvol, divers en internationaal.
Je krijgt ecocheques, internet-connectiviteitsvergoeding en een fietsvergoeding of volledige terugbetaling van je woon-werkverkeer met het openbaar vervoer.
Je werkt grotendeels op campus Groenenborger, in een dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving.
Lees hier meer over werken bij de Universiteit Antwerpen.

Solliciteren?
Je kan tot en met 9 november 2026 voor deze vacature solliciteren via het online sollicitatieplatform van de Universiteit Antwerpen. Klik op de knop ‘Solliciteren’ en vervolledig het online sollicitatieformulier. Voeg  volgende bijlages toe: een motivatiebrief
je academisch cv
een verklaring dat je bereid bent om actief mee te dingen naar bijkomende onderzoeksfinanciering

Het ontbreken van een vereiste bijlage kan leiden tot uitsluiting van de procedure. Sollicitaties via e-mail worden niet in overweging genomen, en kandidaten worden verzocht geen e-mails te sturen louter om te bevestigen dat een sollicitatie via het onlineplatform werd ingediend.
De selectiecommissie bekijkt zo snel mogelijk na de sollicitatiedeadline alle sollicitaties. Zodra er een beslissing genomen is, brengen we je op de hoogte. Als je na de preselectie nog steeds in aanmerking komt, word je geïnformeerd over de eventuele volgende stap(pen) in de selectieprocedure.
De interviews met de geselecteerde kandidaten vinden plaats op 16 november 2026 (ochtend, Antwerpse tijd). De selectiecommissie kan alleen op dit tijdstip bijeenkomen, dus gelieve deze datum alvast in uw agenda te noteren als u naar deze functie solliciteert. Fysieke aanwezigheid heeft de voorkeur, maar indien dit niet mogelijk is, kan een online interview worden geregeld.
Bij vragen over het online sollicitatieformulier kan je de Frequently Asked Questions raadplegen of mailen naar [email protected] . Bij inhoudelijke vragen over de functie kan je contact opnemen met prof. Sammy Verbruggen ( [email protected] ).

De Europese Commissie bekroonde het HR-beleid van de Universiteit Antwerpen met de ‘ HR Excellence in Research Award ’. We zijn een duurzame, gezinsvriendelijke organisatie die maximaal in de groei van medewerkers investeert. We stimuleren diversiteit  en hechten veel belang aan een inclusieve werkomgeving met gelijke kansen - ongeacht gender, functiebeperking, afkomst, levensbeschouwing, seksuele oriëntatie of leeftijd. Wij moedigen mensen met een diverse achtergrond en diverse eigenschappen aan om te solliciteren.

254333.body:
Introduction
Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent.

Job Description
Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real.
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners.
This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. This position is embedded in the Medical Image Analysis group, Department of Biomedical Engineering, TU/e. You will be supervised by dr. Cian Scannell, and co-supervised by prof. Julia Schnabel (TUM).

Job Requirements
A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
Background in deep learning, with an interest in generative models.
Knowledge of MRI physics, physics-based modeling, or inverse problems is a plus.
Proficiency in Python and a deep learning framework such as PyTorch.
A research-oriented attitude, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work in an international, interdisciplinary team, and willingness to spend six months at TUM in Munich.
Strong interest in medical imaging and cardiovascular disease.
Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.
Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
